title: Let Every Mortal Ear Attend
description: Let Every Mortal Ear Attend in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 9 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book I, collected from the Scriptures, hymn 7, headed “The invitation of the gospel; or, Spiritual food and clothing, Isa. 55. 1 &c”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Let ev-ery mor-tal ear at-tend, And ev-ery heart re-joice, The trum-pet of the gos-pel sounds With an i-nvit-ing voice.

lines: The trumpet of the gospel sounds
Ho, all ye hungry starving souls,
And vainly strive with earthly toys
Ho, ye that pant for living streams,
Here you may quench your raging thirst
Rivers of love and mercy here
Like floods of milk and wine.
To weave a garment of your own
That will not hide your sin,
Come naked, and adorn your souls
Wrought by the labours of his Son,
And dy'd in his own blood.
Dear God, the treasures of thy love
Deep as our helpless miseries are,
The happy gates of gospel grace
Lord, we are come to seek supplies,

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
